title: This is a card
subtitle: Every row in the table becomes one of these
body:
## Here's the deal

This is libelli. It turns every row of a spreadsheet into a printed card, and that's the whole trick. The table holds the words, this page holds the design, and you never have to line the two up by hand again.

Go ahead and change *This is a card* in the table. The title changes as you type, because it isn't a copy of the cell — it *is* the cell.

## Import & Export

- **In:** paste cells straight out of Excel, Sheets or Numbers — no header row, no clean-up — or bring a whole file with **Import CSV…**
- **Out:** **Export…** prints the cards or saves each one as a PNG. **Export CSV** saves the words, and **Export** in the template menu saves just the design, small enough to send in a message.

No account, no upload, no server: nothing leaves this browser. Install libelli from your browser and it works offline, or scan the corner to open it on your phone. Want this tour back? **Getting Started** is in the table's menu.
notes: Notes for you, not the reader: this post-it sits **off the page**, so it never prints. The `notes` column fills it.

title: Cells can do more than words
subtitle: Markdown, colour, and the art of leaving things out
body:
## Formatting without a toolbar

Any cell can carry **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `code`, lists, [links](https://heracl.es/libelli) and a rule (`---`, below), and `==two equals signs==` run a ==highlighter== over a few words. Want a few words in colour? Write `[this]{red}` and you get [this]{red}. Hex, `rgb()` and names like [green]{green} or [purple]{purple} all work, and `red` prints as a printer's red rather than your screen's.

That band down the edge is a column too. Type `orange` into this row's `accent` cell and watch it change.

## One cell, many columns

Any cell, and any area's own text, can pull in another column: type `{{` and pick one from the list, and `{{column}}` is replaced by whatever this row holds there. This card is called *{{title}}*, and nobody had to type that twice. Add a find and a replace, `{{column:find:replace}}`, and it changes on the way in: swap *words* for *that* in this title and it reads *{{title:words:that}}*. The squiggle under `{{column}}` means no column has that name; it never prints.

---

## Notice what's missing

This row has no link, so **there's no QR code in the corner**. An area set to *Hide When Empty* gets out of the way instead of leaving a hole.
notes: Check the colours on real paper before printing all of them — a printer's red is never a screen's.

title: Nothing on this page is stuck
subtitle: Drag it, restyle it, or start over from your own columns
body:
## Everything moves

The design starts **locked**, so the tour can't be knocked out of place by accident — the padlock beside the page, above the area button, unlocks it. Then drag any area, or grab a corner to resize it. Make this title absurdly long and the text below moves down, because it's anchored to the title rather than pinned in place. Run out of room and the area's corner turns red, so you find out before the printer does.

## Style is per area

That stamp is a drawing stored in the row itself, turned a few degrees, its perforated border drawn by hand and its shadow cast by the template's own CSS. Double-click it to draw your own.

Even the paragraphs have a style: these are told apart by an indent rather than a gap, measured in lines of leading. Select anything and the bar above shows how it's made.

## Keep more than one design

The caret beside **Template** holds every design you save, and **A5 Starter** there brings this one back as it came. Start a new one and the button with three shapes reads your columns and lays out a first draft for you.
notes: Try it: unlock the page, then drag the stamp somewhere it shouldn't be.

title: Take it with you
subtitle: On paper, as a picture, or as a booklet
body:
## Print it

Hit **Export…** or Ctrl/Cmd+P for a preview of every sheet. Turn on background graphics so the colours make it onto the paper. The date in the footer fills itself in on the day you print.

## Or fold it into a zine

These four cards make exactly one booklet. They already have left and right pages, which is why the page numbers sit on the outside edge.

1. In the preview, set **Pages per Sheet** to **2-up** and **Order** to **Zine**.
2. Print double-sided, flipping on the long edge.
3. Fold it in half. Congratulations, you made a zine.
notes: Print one test sheet first. Double-sided is easy to get backwards.
